description: AI agent toolkit: unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI, coding agent CLI

summary.one_liner: Pi is a minimal, extensible TypeScript agent harness with a unified multi-provider LLM API, an agent runtime, a terminal UI library, and an interactive coding agent CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Pi is a monorepo containing the Pi CLI and supporting libraries: pi-ai (unified LLM API across providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google), pi-agent-core (agent runtime with tool calling and state management), pi-tui (terminal UI with differential rendering), and pi-coding-agent (the interactive coding agent CLI). Other listed packages cover a typed host runtime with hot-reloadable plugins (chord), telemetry contracts (pi-telemetry), and durable conversation, task and document storage (pi-durable). The CLI can be used interactively, in print or JSON mode for automation, over RPC, or through the TypeScript SDK. Customization is done through extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, which can be bundled as packages and shared via npm or git. The README states that Pi deliberately omits built-in sub-agents and plan mode, leaving those to user-built extensions or packages.
use_cases: run an AI coding agent in a project directory from the terminal
automate coding tasks in print or JSON mode
control a coding agent over RPC
build an app on a TypeScript SDK for LLM agents
call many LLM providers through one API
build a terminal UI with differential rendering
sandbox a coding agent in Docker or a micro-VM
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | sh  (macOS/Linux installer; URL missing from README text)
/login (inside Pi, to connect a subscription or API key)
notable: Customizable via extensions, skills, prompt templates and themes, shareable as npm or git packages
Supply-chain hardening: exact-pinned direct deps, min-release-age, install lock generated from root lockfile, --ignore-scripts installs
Multiple run modes: interactive, print/JSON for automation, RPC, and TypeScript SDK
Offline Nix builds using a pinned model catalog revision
Local tooling to consume built packages from outside the monorepo
caveats: No built-in permission system; runs with the launching user's filesystem, process, network and credential access, so sandboxing must be added separately (README lists Gondolin, Docker and OpenShell patterns)
Sub-agents and plan mode are intentionally not included by default
npm install does not pin transitive dependencies; the pinned installer is the option for that
